pages.text: "I want to drink by myself!" Nia stood by the water and lowered their long neck. Their mouth was still far above it. "Why can't I reach?"
"Here goes!" Nia spread their front feet a little and lowered their neck. Their feet slid in the dirt! Again—and another slip! "Why won't it work?" Their ears drooped.
Ten tries, ten slips. Nia retreated to the acacia shade and sat down. "I can't. Only I can't do it." Tears gathered in their eyes.
Mom and Tumba came over. "Everyone starts like that!" Mom nuzzled Nia's cheek. "Spread your front feet farther. If it doesn't work, spread your feet and try again!" Tumba echoed her.
Mom explained, "Too far all at once makes you slip. A little farther than yesterday." Tumba drew a line beside Nia's foot with their snout. "This far today!" Nia's ears perked.
Back at the shore, Nia spread their feet to the line and lowered their neck. Almost touching! A little short, but no slip! "I didn't fall!" Tumba waved their tail. Spread your feet, try again!
The next day, Tumba drew a line a little farther out. Nia slid and muddied their knees, but didn't cry. "It's okay. Spread your feet, try again!" Nia grinned with muddy knees.
Another day, another wider line. Nia spread their front feet and lowered their neck. Splash! Their mouth reached water. Cool gulps ran down their throat. Dripping and swaying, Nia cried, "I drank!"

All three made a promise. "One, it's okay if it doesn't work at first! Two, spread your feet and try again! Three, a little farther than yesterday!" Lines widened day by day in the dirt. "More water tomorrow!" Nia called.
Mom leaned her side against Nia's legs. "Drinking on your own—wonderful!" Tumba nuzzled Nia's hoof. Trying again helped a little at a time. Spread your feet, try again!
